request: can you show me why a negative times a negative is positive?

beats.intent: An arrow from 0 to 2 on a number line stretching out to 6
beats.narration: Think of multiplying as doing something to an arrow. Times three stretches the arrow for two out to six.
beats.code:
stage.title("Negative times negative")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(-6, 6, 1))
o = nl.n2p(0) + 0.5 * UP
a = draw_arrow(stage, o, nl.n2p(2) + 0.5 * UP)
stage.play(Transform(a, Arrow(o, nl.n2p(6) + 0.5 * UP, buff=0, color=YELLOW)), run_time=1.5)
stage.caption("3 × 2: stretch the arrow to 6")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A green arrow for 2 swinging round to point at -2
beats.narration: Times minus one turns the arrow around. Two becomes minus two.
beats.code:
stage.clear(keep=[nl])
b = draw_arrow(stage, o, nl.n2p(2) + 0.5 * UP, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Rotate(b, PI, about_point=o), run_time=1.5)
stage.caption("Times -1: turn around, 2 becomes -2")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The backwards arrow stretching to -6
beats.narration: Now times three stretches that backwards arrow: three times minus two is minus six.
beats.code:
stage.play(Transform(b, Arrow(o, nl.n2p(-6) + 0.5 * UP, buff=0, color=GREEN)), run_time=1.5)
stage.caption("3 × (-2) = -6: stretched the other way")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The -6 arrow turning around once more to land on +6
beats.narration: Multiply by minus one again and the arrow turns around a second time. Two turnarounds face forward: plus six.
beats.code:
stage.play(Rotate(b, PI, about_point=o), run_time=1.5)
highlight(stage, b)
stage.caption("Turn around twice: facing forward, +6")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: Dots on the line y = -2x, climbing by 2 as x steps left past zero
beats.narration: Or follow a pattern. Each time x drops by one, x times minus two goes up by two, and it keeps going past zero.
beats.code:
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-3, 3, 1), y_range=(-6, 6, 2))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: -2 * x, color=GREEN)
pts = VGroup(*[Dot(ax.c2p(x, -2 * x), color=YELLOW) for x in (3, 2, 1, 0, -1, -2, -3)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(d) for d in pts], lag_ratio=0.3), run_time=2.5)
stage.caption("x × (-2): up by 2 each step left")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The pattern of products written out beside the line, ending at +2
beats.narration: Two, one, zero, minus one, times minus two: minus four, minus two, zero, and then plus two. Nothing else fits.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"2 \times (-2) = -4", r"1 \times (-2) = -2", r"0 \times (-2) = 0", r"(-1) \times (-2) = 2", where="right")
stage.caption("The pattern forces the answer: positive")
stage.pause(2)

request: what does it actually mean for a function to be continuous

beats.intent: A smooth wave traced by a dot from end to end without a break
beats.narration: A continuous function is one you can draw without lifting your pen.
beats.code:
stage.title("Continuous functions")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6, 1), y_range=(0, 4, 1))
f = lambda x: 2 + np.sin(x)
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, f)
trace_graph(stage, ax, f, 0, 6)
stage.caption("Draw it without lifting your pen")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A step that jumps from height 1 to height 3 at x = 3, an open circle at the gap
beats.narration: Here is one that is not. At x equals three it jumps from one up to three.
beats.code:
ax2 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6, 1), y_range=(0, 4, 1))
lo = plot_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: 1, x_range=(0, 3))
hi = plot_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: 3, x_range=(3, 6))
hole = Circle(radius=0.09, color=BLUE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(ax2.c2p(3, 1))
full = Dot(ax2.c2p(3, 3), color=BLUE)
stage.play(FadeIn(hole), FadeIn(full))
stage.caption("At x = 3 it jumps: the pen lifts")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: Two dots sliding toward x = 3, one from each side, stopping at different heights
beats.narration: Walk toward three from the left and the height heads to one. From the right it heads to three. They disagree.
beats.code:
trace_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: 1, 0.5, 2.9, color=GREEN, run_time=2)
trace_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: 3, 5.5, 3.1, color=RED, run_time=2)
stage.caption("From the left: 1. From the right: 3")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The line y = x + 2 with a single point missing at x = 2
beats.narration: Another way to fail: x squared minus four, over x minus two, is the line x plus two, except at x equals two, where it is undefined.
beats.code:
ax3 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 5, 1), y_range=(0, 7, 1))
g3 = plot_graph(stage, ax3, lambda x: x + 2)
gap = Circle(radius=0.09, color=BLUE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(ax3.c2p(2, 4))
stage.play(FadeIn(gap))
highlight(stage, gap)
stage.caption("Undefined at x = 2: a hole in the curve")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The hole plugged with a yellow dot at (2, 4)
beats.narration: Both sides head to four. Define the value there as four and the hole closes.
beats.code:
plug = Dot(ax3.c2p(2, 4), color=YELLOW, radius=0.1)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(plug))
pulse(stage, plug)
stage.caption("Set f(2) = 4 and the hole closes")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The definition of continuity beside the mended line
beats.narration: That is the definition: where the function is heading equals where it actually is.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a)", where="right")
stage.caption("Continuous: the limit equals the value")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A tangent sliding along the line, its slope reading 0.50 the whole way

beats.intent: A steeper red line y = 2x - 1 with a step of 1 across and 2 up
beats.narration: A steeper line has a bigger slope. This one climbs two for every one across: slope two.

stage.clear(keep=[ax, g])
g2 = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 2 * x - 1, x_range=(0.5, 3.5), color=RED)
r2 = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(2, 3), ax.c2p(3, 3), color=GREEN)
u2 = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(3, 3), ax.c2p(3, 5), color=YELLOW)
stage.caption("Slope 2: up 2 for every 1 across")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: An orange line y = 5 - x falling to the right
beats.narration: A line that falls as you go right has a negative slope. This one drops one for every one across.
beats.code:

d3 = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(1, 4), ax.c2p(2, 4), color=GREEN)
e3 = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(2, 4), ax.c2p(2, 3), color=ORANGE)
stage.caption("Falling to the right: slope -1")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The rise-over-run formula worked out for the first line
beats.narration: In symbols: the change in y over the change in x. For our first line, two over four, one half.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"m = \frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}", r"m = \frac{3.5 - 1.5}{5 - 1} = 0.5", where="right")
stage.pause(2)

request: show me what integration actually is

beats.intent: A speed curve v = 0.1t² + 1 over five seconds
beats.narration: Say your speed changes over five seconds like this curve. How far did you go?
beats.code:
stage.title("What integration is")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 5, 1), y_range=(0, 4, 1), labels=("t", "v"))
f = lambda t: 0.1 * t ** 2 + 1
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, f)
stage.caption("Speed over 5 seconds: how far did we go?")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: Five rectangles under the curve, one per second
beats.narration: Pretend the speed is constant for each second. Each strip is speed times time, a little distance. They add to eight.
beats.code:
rects = riemann_refine(stage, ax, g, 0, 5, ns=(5,))
stage.caption("Each strip: speed × time. Total 8.0")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The strips splitting into 10, 20 and 40 thinner ones
beats.narration: Use thinner strips and the staircase hugs the curve. With forty strips the total is nine point zero one.
beats.code:
stage.clear(keep=[ax, g])
rects2 = riemann_refine(stage, ax, g, 0, 5, ns=(5, 10, 20, 40))
stage.caption("40 strips: 9.01, closing in")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The whole area under the curve shaded solid
beats.narration: In the limit the strips become the exact area under the curve: fifty-five sixths, about nine point one seven.
beats.code:
stage.clear(keep=[ax, g])
area = shade_area(stage, ax, g, 0, 5)
stage.caption("The exact area: 55/6, about 9.17")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The running total A(t) climbing as a dot traces it to 9.17
beats.narration: Integration also gives the running total: the distance covered up to each moment.
beats.code:
ax2 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 5, 1), y_range=(0, 10, 2), labels=("t", "A"))
F = lambda t: t ** 3 / 30 + t
G = plot_graph(stage, ax2, F, color=YELLOW)
trace_graph(stage, ax2, F, 0, 5)
end = mark_point(stage, ax2, (5, 55 / 6), color=RED, label="9.17", direction=LEFT)
stage.caption("Distance so far: the area up to each t")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The integral evaluated beside the running total
beats.narration: Written as an integral: the sum of speed times a tiny time, from zero to five, is fifty-five sixths.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\int_0^5 (0.1t^2 + 1)\,dt", r"\int_0^5 (0.1t^2 + 1)\,dt = \frac{125}{30} + 5 = \frac{55}{6}", where="right")
stage.pause(2)

request: why do we even care about eigenvalues?

beats.intent: Four coloured arrows on the grid before a matrix acts
beats.narration: Here are four arrows. Watch where each one points when a matrix moves the plane.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why eigenvalues matter")
p = draw_plane(stage)
a = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 0), color=GREEN)
b = draw_vector(stage, p, (0, 1), color=RED)
c = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 1), color=YELLOW)
d = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, -1), color=TEAL)
stage.caption("Watch the direction of each arrow")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The grid moved by [[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]]: green and red turn, yellow and teal keep their lines
beats.narration: Green and red get knocked off their lines. Yellow doubles in length and teal does not move at all.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]], riders=[a, b, c, d])
stage.caption("Yellow and teal only stretch: they don't turn")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A fresh grid with the matrix's two eigen-lines, arrows on them staying put
beats.narration: Those special directions are the eigenvectors. Arrows on them only stretch, and the stretch factor is the eigenvalue.
beats.code:
p2 = draw_plane(stage)
show_eigenvectors(stage, p2, [[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]])
stage.caption("Eigenvectors: stretched, never turned")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The eigenvalue equation and the two eigenvalues beside the grid
beats.narration: A times v equals lambda times v. Along one one the stretch is two, along one minus one it is one.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"A\vec v = \lambda \vec v", r"\lambda = 2 \text{ on } (1, 1), \quad \lambda = 1 \text{ on } (1, -1)", where="right")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: An arrow's direction after 0 to 5 pushes by the matrix, fanning onto the λ = 2 line
beats.narration: Here is why they matter. Apply the matrix again and again: any arrow swings round onto the eigenvalue-two line.
beats.code:
p3 = draw_plane(stage)
ln = draw_span(stage, p3, (1, 1), color=YELLOW)
A = np.array([[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]])
dirs = [np.linalg.matrix_power(A, k) @ np.array([2, -1]) for k in range(6)]
fan = VGroup(*[Arrow(p3.c2p(0, 0), p3.c2p(*(2.5 * v / np.linalg.norm(v))), buff=0, color=interpolate_color(RED, YELLOW, k / 5)) for k, v in enumerate(dirs)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(x) for x in fan], lag_ratio=0.7), run_time=4)
stage.caption("Push after push: pulled onto the λ = 2 line")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The long-run rule beside the fanned arrows
beats.narration: After many steps the biggest eigenvalue wins. Populations, page rankings and vibrations all settle this way.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"A^n \vec x \approx 2^n\, c_1 \vec v_1", where="right")
stage.caption("The biggest eigenvalue decides the long run")
stage.pause(2)

beats.code:
stage.title("Bubble sort")
bars = draw_array(stage, [5, 2, 8, 1, 6, 3])
stage.caption("Six numbers, out of order")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The first two bars, 5 and 2, compared and swapped
beats.narration: Compare the first two. Five is bigger than two, so they swap.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, VGroup(bars[0], bars[1]))
swap_bars(stage, bars, 0, 1)
stage.caption("5 > 2: swap them")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The 8 swapping rightward past 1, 6 and 3 to the end, turning green
beats.narration: Keep walking right. The eight keeps winning its comparisons and bubbles all the way to the end, where it belongs.
beats.code:
swap_bars(stage, bars, 2, 3)
swap_bars(stage, bars, 3, 4)
swap_bars(stage, bars, 4, 5)
stage.play(bars[5].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.9), run_time=0.6)
stage.caption("Pass 1: the 8 bubbles to the end")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A second pass swapping 5 with 1 and 6 with 3, the 6 turning green
beats.narration: Second pass: five passes one, six passes three, and the six settles into place.
beats.code:
swap_bars(stage, bars, 1, 2)
swap_bars(stage, bars, 3, 4)
stage.play(bars[4].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.9), run_time=0.6)
stage.caption("Pass 2: the 6 settles")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A third pass swapping 2 with 1 and 5 with 3, every bar green
beats.narration: Third pass: two passes one, five passes three. Now everything is in order.
beats.code:
swap_bars(stage, bars, 0, 1)
swap_bars(stage, bars, 2, 3)
stage.play(*[bars[k].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.9) for k in range(6)], run_time=0.8)
stage.caption("Pass 3: sorted, 1 2 3 5 6 8")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The number of comparisons counted beside the sorted bars
beats.narration: In the worst case it compares five, then four, three, two, one pairs: n times n minus one over two, fifteen here.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\text{comparisons} = 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1", r"\text{comparisons} = \tfrac{n(n-1)}{2} = 15", where="right")
stage.caption("Double the list: about four times the work")
stage.pause(2)

request: can you show me what a limit is

beats.intent: The curve sin x / x with an open circle where x = 0
beats.narration: Here is sine x over x. At zero it is zero over zero: no value at all.
beats.code:
stage.title("What a limit is")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-8, 8, 2), y_range=(-0.5, 1.5, 0.5))
f = lambda x: np.sinc(x / PI)
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, f)
hole = Circle(radius=0.09, color=BLUE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(ax.c2p(0, 1))
stage.play(FadeIn(hole))
stage.caption("sin(x)/x has no value at x = 0")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: Two dots riding the curve in from both sides toward the hole
beats.narration: But walk toward zero from either side and the height closes in on one.
beats.code:
trace_graph(stage, ax, f, -7, -0.1, color=GREEN, run_time=2.5)
trace_graph(stage, ax, f, 7, 0.1, color=RED, run_time=2.5)
stage.caption("From both sides the height heads to 1")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A zoomed view between -0.5 and 0.5, the curve still heading to the hole at 1
beats.narration: Zoom in as far as you like. The values get closer and closer to one, and never need the value at zero.
beats.code:
ax2 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-0.5, 0.5, 0.25), y_range=(0.95, 1.01, 0.01))
g2 = plot_graph(stage, ax2, f)
hole2 = Circle(radius=0.09, color=BLUE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(ax2.c2p(0, 1))
stage.play(FadeIn(hole2))
stage.caption("Zoomed in: still heading to 1")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The limit written beside the zoomed curve
beats.narration: That is the limit: the value the function heads toward, not the value it has there.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin x}{x} = 1", where="right")
stage.caption("Where it heads, not where it is")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A wobbling curve settling toward 1, a green band around 1 narrowing
beats.narration: Limits at infinity work the same way. However narrow a band you draw around one, far enough out the curve stays inside it.
beats.code:
ax3 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 20, 2), y_range=(0, 2, 0.5))
h = lambda x: 1 + 2 * np.sin(x) / (x + 1)
gh = plot_graph(stage, ax3, h)
band = narrow_epsilon_band(stage, ax3, gh, 1, eps=0.6, shrink_to=0.15)
stage.caption("Any band around 1: far out, the curve stays in")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The limit at infinity written beside the band
beats.narration: We write it as the limit of the function as x goes to infinity, equal to one.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\lim_{x \to \infty} \left(1 + \frac{2\sin x}{x + 1}\right) = 1", where="right")
stage.pause(2)
